question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:**

After the heavy rain, the floodwaters rose___________ the level of the streets,
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. above .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes the rise of floodwaters in relation to the level of the streets. A preposition is required to establish this relationship.
 
• The preposition **"above"** is used to indicate a higher position or level in comparison to something else.
 
• In this context, the floodwaters rose higher than the streets, making **"above"** the most appropriate preposition.

Correct sentence: *After the heavy rain, the floodwaters rose **above** the level of the streets*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**
 
 
• **Below:** Refers to a lower position or level (e.g., "The basement is below the ground.").
 
• **Across:** Indicates movement from one side to another or spanning an area (e.g., "The bridge goes across the river.").
 
• **Between:** Used to refer to a position or state separating two things (e.g., "The shop is between the bakery and the pharmacy.").
 
 
 
• **Why "Above" is Correct:** It precisely conveys the idea of floodwaters rising higher than the streets, which aligns with the intended meaning of the sentence.
